traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and explicit requirements from docs/stories/010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS.story.md are fully implemented and verified: - The valid-annotation-format rule supports both nested (story/req) and flat (storyPathPattern/requirementIdPattern) configuration for custom regex patterns, with corresponding example strings used in error messages. - Defaults match the original hardcoded behavior when no options are provided or when invalid regex patterns are supplied, ensuring backward compatibility. - Regex patterns are validated at configuration time; invalid patterns produce clear configuration errors via the invalidRuleConfiguration message while the rule safely falls back to defaults. - Configuration is defined via a JSON Schema-compatible meta.schema that aligns with ESLint best practices, including type checks and additionalProperties: false for both nested and flat options. - Validation and error message helpers (buildStoryErrorMessage, buildReqErrorMessage, validateStoryAnnotation, validateReqAnnotation) respect the configured patterns and examples. - A comprehensive Jest test suite explicitly tied to this story exercises valid and invalid configurations, example overrides, nested vs flat precedence, and fallback behavior, and all those tests pass. - User-facing documentation in user-docs/api-reference.md clearly describes how to configure storyPathPattern, requirementIdPattern, and their example fields, and how these options interact with other rules, satisfying the documentation and integration criteria.
Based on this concrete code, tests, and documentation evidence, the story 010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS is fully implemented and passes.
